prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance toward the right front corner, draws uke firmly against his own right chest, and, pivoting on the left foot, swings the back of the right thigh in from the front between uke's legs, springing up from the inside and throwing uke forward.

Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall). Uke's cooperation: Uke is thrown while arching the upper body an appropriate amount, so that tori does not end up bent forward. How to take the ukemi: Uke matches tori's uchi-mata and takes mae-mawari-ukemi (forward rolling breakfall). Tori, using a forward-turning tai-sabaki (body movement), breaks uke's balance to the front, springs up from the inside with the right leg, and throws uke forward.

heading.en: Introductory way of applying the technique

prose.en: How to take the ukemi: Uke rotates sideways, pivoting on the right knee, and takes yoko-ukemi (side breakfall). Tori breaks the balance of uke: who is up on one knee: to the front, and throws by springing up from the inside with the right leg.
While uke is turning to the right, throw in response to that movement.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori must not step in shallowly with the supporting leg and try to throw with the leg alone.
Do not apply the technique bent forward, in a posture that drives the head into the tatami.
